newsitem.title: USA: Yellen says sees no precursors to U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Yellen says sees no precursors to U.S. inflation.

text.p: Janet Yellen, who chairs the White House Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), said on Wednesday that U.S. inflation is clearly under control and that she sees no signs of the precursors to any pick-up.

She also told reporters U.S. growth was likely to slow to a more sustainable pace than the first quarter's 5.6 percent, adding that U.S. fiscal policy and net exports were likely to prove a drag on the economy. Yellen said it is appropriate to watch for overheating in the U.S. economy, though she saw no signs of a build-up in inflation, and that she did not see an unsustainable build-up in the U.S. current account deficit.

"I think we're at a point where it's appropriate to watch out for overheating and to be monitoring the economy for overheating but I haven't seen any signs at this point of a pick-up in inflation or the precursors to a pick-up in inflation," Yellen told reporters.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Commerce Department reported that the U.S. economy grew at an unexpectedly strong 5.6 percent in the first quarter.

Yellen said there was "reason to believe that growth going forward is likely to moderate to a more sustainable pace," adding that net exports and the government's fiscal policy were likely to be a drag on the economy's growth.
"Looking forward, my sense is that we are likely to see continued growth with low inflation for the remainder of the year," Yellen said.

"Probably consumer spending will return to a more normal pace and I would think the same is probably true for business investment, but we've got an expansion that looks like it still has a long way to go," she said.
